summary: Reserved capacity GPU exhaustion causes batched request failures and latency spikes
description: Issue summary: BrightCart observed a sharp increase in 5xx errors and token latency for requests routed to their reserved pool between 2026-03-12T09:40 and 2026-03-12T11:05 UTC. Impact: ~22% of batched requests returned 500/502 within the window, median token latency increased from ~45ms to ~420ms, and several long-running streams were terminated by the serving runtime. Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool id rp-44), prod us-east-1, cluster sku: 8xA100, autoscale policy: conservative-burst-v2. Steps: See steps_to_reproduce. Logs and telemetry attached below. Initial hypothesis: sudden saturation of GPU memory/KV cache by a single noisy tenant causing eviction storms and scheduler thrashing, which cascaded to failed batch allocations and queue timeouts. Resolution summary: applied temporary isolation by moving the noisy tenant to a different pool, increased pool GPU headroom and lowered max_batch_size for affected routes, and deployed an autoscaler fix to back-pressure noisy-tenant allocation. Follow-ups: post-incident audit of tenant scheduling and new quota-based scheduling enforcement.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send 100 concurrent batched requests (batch size 16) to /v1/generate on BrightCart's reserved pool rp-44 using open-7b-q4 model.
2) Observe request queue growth beyond configured max_queue_ms and increased token generation latency after ~15 minutes.
3) Repeat with a single high-memory streaming workload (long context, prefix cache hits) to replicate KV cache eviction pattern.
4) Monitor metrics: gpu_utilization, gpu_memory_used, serving_batch_alloc_errors, scheduler_queue_length.
5) Confirm 5xx error spike aligns with GPU memory OOM and batch allocation failures in logs.

comments: Support (Maya): Customer reported recurring ~20% 5xx rate for batched routes starting ~09:40 UTC. Provided initial logs and requested SRE assistance. Link to Slack thread: #support-brightcart (slack.com/archives/C02ABC/ppp456)

SRE (Diego): Began live investigation at 09:55 UTC. Noted high GPU memory pressure across 3 nodes and repeated KV cache evictions. Hypothesis: one tenant's streaming workload retained large prefix caches causing memory blowout and preventing new batch allocations.
Customer (BrightCart - Alice Mills): Confirms a background evaluation job ramped up in the morning that cycles long-context prompts every 30s. Will pause job if that helps.

SRE (Diego): Paused suspected tenant workload at 10:07 UTC and observed immediate drop in eviction rate and allocation failures. Initiated tenant isolation and scaled rp-44 headroom +1 GPU as temporary mitigation.
Support (Maya): Notified customer of mitigation and timeline. Customer validated reduced errors after job pause.

Engineering (Priya - autoscaler): Deployed autoscaler hotfix at 10:52 UTC to prevent scale prevention loop when pool reports high allocation failures. Patch: prioritize new allocation slots over deferring scale-up when allocation failures > threshold.
SRE (Diego): Closed incident at 11:05 UTC after stabilization and rollback of temporary measures to standard config with quota enforcement enabled.
Postmortem reminder: Owner assigned for follow-ups: Priya Khatri (autoscaler), Diego Alvarez (scheduling), Maya Chen (CS liaison)
investigation_notes: Metric analysis: serving_batch_alloc_errors correlated with gpu_memory_used > 92% and KV eviction spikes. Three nodes (rp-44-node-3/5/7) showed repeated allocation timeouts.
Heap: The noisy tenant's streaming workload retained large KV caches (~8GB per worker) due to long-context inference pattern and lacked prefix caching TTL in user config.
Scheduler behavior: When allocation timeouts occurred, scheduler attempted to rebalance batches which increased queue delay and caused downstream 502s from timeouts.

Autoscaler observation: conservative-burst-v2 policy prevented immediate scale-up because it evaluates aggregated queue signal and saw transient oscillation; this created a feedback loop where allocation failures blocked scale triggers.
Customer config: BrightCart had max_batch_size=64 and aggressive prefetch settings; lowering batch size reduced per-batch memory and improved headroom.
Related incidents: SUP-51777 documented intermittent GPU availability that had similar symptoms but different root cause (eviction due to kernel memory leak). Linked for historical context.
resolution: Applied temporary tenant isolation by moving the noisy evaluation job to a separate reserved pool, increased pool headroom by adding one GPU to rp-44 for 1 hour, lowered max_batch_size for the affected routes to 16, and deployed an autoscaler patch to break the prevention loop. Customer confirmed error rate returned to baseline and median token latency dropped back under 70ms. Incident marked resolved after 30m of stable metrics.
follow_up_actions: 1) Enforce per-tenant KV-cache memory quotas in the serving-runtime (Owner: Diego) - target ETA 2026-03-26
2) Add quota-based scheduling to autoscaler to avoid allocation/prevention loops (Owner: Priya) - target ETA 2026-03-19
3) Update dedicated capacity onboarding checklist to include recommended max_batch_size and prefix TTL settings for streaming workloads (Owner: Maya) - target ETA 2026-03-18
4) Run a synthetic soak test for rp-44 configuration to validate the autoscaler fix under long-context streaming patterns (Owner: SRE) - scheduled 2026-03-15
5) Customer follow-up call to review best-practices and configuration changes (Owner: CS) - scheduled 2026-03-14
